parties: Bosch Home Comfort India Limited (promoter); NSE-listed company
headline: Bosch Home Comfort India Limited: Promoter Offer for Sale (OFS) of Shares
sum: Bosch Home Comfort India Limited's promoter initiated an Offer for Sale (OFS) of company shares, constituting a substantial change in promoter holding as mandated under Regulation 30 of SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015.
implication: OFS transactions by promoters typically signal capital redeployment or strategic stake dilution post-listing; the transaction mechanics and lock-in compliance will be material to minority shareholder protection and market conduct.
detail: The promoter of BHCIL notified the National Stock Exchange of India (NSE) of a proposed sale of shares through an Offer for Sale mechanism on June 24, 2026. The OFS is a structured off-market sale permitting promoters to divest shares while maintaining price discovery and regulatory oversight. The announcement was filed under NSE Regulation 30 (substantial changes in shareholding), indicating the stake reduction met materiality thresholds. Specific share count, discount/premium to market price, and final settlement details are not disclosed in the available public source.

framework.ref: SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015, Regulation 30
framework.note: central: mandates immediate disclosure of substantial changes in shareholding and promoter/key management transactions to stock exchanges and public

framework.ref: SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015, Sections 3–4
framework.note: central: restricts promoter/insider share sales during closed periods unless exempted; OFS must comply with trading window restrictions

framework.ref: Companies Act, 2013, Section 65 (OFS mechanics) & Rule 5 (transfer of shares)
framework.note: central: governs offer for sale mechanisms and share transfer procedures in listed company context

framework.ref: SEBI (Substantial Acquisition of Shares and Takeovers) Regulations, 2011, Regulation 3–4 & Schedule 4
framework.note: applies if promoter stake drops below threshold triggering open offer exemption thresholds; disclosure of acquirer identity required in certain cases

framework.ref: Securities Contracts (Regulation) Act, 1956, Section 23 & Rules thereunder
framework.note: governs conduct of OFS and settlement through registered brokers/clearing houses on stock exchange

framework.ref: Companies Act, 2013, Section 43 & Rule 7 (beneficial ownership & pledging)
framework.note: restricts promoter dealings with pledged shares; OFS requires confirmation of free ownership unless part of structured transaction

framework.ref: Income Tax Act, 1961, Section 94 (transfer of shares) & Section 56 (capital gains)
framework.note: promoter liable for capital gains tax on sale; applicable only to promoter as seller, not regulatory gate

conditions: Promoter shareholding must remain above threshold or trigger mandatory disclosure under Regulation 31 (if applicable)
No trading window closure violations; sale must occur outside blackout periods for insiders
NSE and BSE approval/consent if required under exchange bye-laws
Delivery and settlement of shares within T+2 rolling settlement cycle
structure.novel: OFS in a recently listed (or newly demerged) Bosch Group subsidiary; likely first major promoter divestment post-listing; structure preserves price discovery through exchange OFS mechanism rather than block deal.

triggers.note: OFS requires mandatory immediate disclosure to stock exchange and public; triggers investor notification and market scrutiny
promoter/insider sales subject to trading window restrictions and blackout period compliance; exemptions must be pre-cleared
if promoter stake drops below 20%, potential open offer exemption review and acquirer identity disclosure requirements
